# `iscope_start_stack`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start the stacking stage of the star view, optionally clearing the previous stack.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (full command-socket call; shared diagnostic writes; 64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xddcd0 (64-bit build) |

Starts (or, if already running, leaves running) the Stack stage on the star view. A success reply does not mean a new stack was started or that stacking finished; when Stack is already running and restart is not true the call can return success without restarting. On wide-camera setups the request may be relayed to the other camera process and the relayed reply returned. The grade reflects the whole request/reply path, which reaches the shared diagnostic logger; it does not by itself mean the method changes device settings.

Side effects: Clears the stack when restart is true and Stack is idle; sets or clears the continue-stack flag and exposure override (64-bit build); stops the previous view, switches to star mode, clears subframe state and starts the Stack worker asynchronously; may relay to the second camera process. Every call also performs shared request/reply diagnostic logging.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"iscope_start_stack"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional object. Absent, null, scalar or array params are treated as no keys and the stack stage is still started. A positional array wrapping the object is ignored. Unknown keys ignored. [READ] |
| `params.restart` | boolean\|integer | no | no restart; continue flag differs from explicit false (64-bit build) | Optional boolean or integer (nonzero true). True: if Stack is already running the call fails with 259, otherwise the stack is cleared first. In the 64-bit build an explicit false (continue) and an omitted or malformed value set different internal continue flags, so a client wanting to continue SHOULD send false explicitly. [READ] |
| `params.main_stack_exp_us` | integer | no | -1 | 64-bit build only: optional integer, read only for the wide-camera process; missing or wrong type gives -1, values <= 0 normalise to -1. Microseconds (INFERRED from the name). Not read by the 32-bit handler; not sent by the app. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 259 | restart evaluates true and Stack is already running (checked before clearing) | `stack is already running` |
| 318 | Camera is not open | `device not connected` |
| 212 | Worker function missing or thread creation failed | `fail to create thread` |
| 300 | Relay to the other process has no user-data context | `internal error` |
| 207 | A failure left the error code zero | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No ViewPlan-running guard appears in this handler. Other worker and driver error codes are not established.

## Example

Request, continue - Continue stacking, explicit false:

```json
{"id":41,"method":"iscope_start_stack","params":{"restart":false}}
```

Request, restart - Clear and restart:

```json
{"id":42,"method":"iscope_start_stack","params":{"restart":true}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"iscope_start_stack","result":0,"code":0,"id":41}
```

Reply, already-running:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"iscope_start_stack","error":"stack is already running","code":259,"id":43}
```
